description: Agent fix hints for EasyScanPKG Sonar findings (pair with .sft/issue-checklist.md).

python:S3516.summary: Method always returns the same value
guidance: Return meaningful distinct values for success vs failure paths
Or change the function to void/None if the return is unused
Check fail-open hooks: returning True always hides failures
Extract nested branches into named helpers
Use early returns / guard clauses
Split multi-responsibility functions; target complexity ≤ 15
Introduce a module-level named constant near first use
Reuse the constant everywhere the literal appeared
Replace nested x if c else y if d else z with if/elif/else statements
Or extract a small helper that returns the chosen value
If catching Exception (or a parent), drop child types already covered
Keep only the most specific types you need to handle differently
Rename to _ if the value is intentionally ignored
Or remove the assignment if truly unused
Merge nested if A: if B: into if A and B:
Replace broken regex (e.g. .*? that can only match empty) with a correct pattern
Prefer explicit character classes over reluctant dots when intent is clear
Pass the iterable directly if only iterating once
Keep list() only when you need random access, len, or multiple passes
Localhost IDE/Sonar bridges may intentionally use http://127.0.0.1 — document why
For non-loopback hosts prefer https://
If intentional, keep the finding listed; do not 'resolve' without rationale
Do not use an object after std::move / move construction unless it was reassigned
Prefer copying when both the original and the new owner need a valid value
Reset or reinitialize the moved-from object before further use
Check has_value()/operator bool before operator* or value()
Prefer value_or(...) when a default is acceptable
Guard pointer use with null checks
Prefer references or gsl::not_null when null is not a valid state
Add braces to if/for/while bodies for clarity and safer edits
Validate buffer sizes and pointer lifetimes before dereference
Watch for off-by-one errors and use-after-free
Reproduce under Dr. Memory with a small failing command from scan policy
Initialize locals and buffers before read
Zero-fill malloc'd memory when contents are read before write
Free every malloc/new on all exit paths
Prefer RAII (unique_ptr/shared_ptr) over raw owning pointers
Do not free the same pointer twice
Only free pointers obtained from the matching allocator
